judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard integration and precedence clause; the only soft edge is the phrase 'inconsistent with this Agreement', which is a familiar and workable formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its precedence rule ('this Agreement shall govern') sits against Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1, which resolves inconsistencies by requiring the better quality/greater quantity as the Architect interprets, and against the Addendum's revisions, so a court could have to reconcile two different conflict-resolution regimes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; 'except to the extent specifically indicated' is anchored to the Contract Documents themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum expressly replaces Article 2 with a revised version, so the original is superseded rather than in conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The inserted date is 'Approximately the Fifteenth of July', and an approximate commencement date is inherently imprecise for measuring the Contract Time.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum 4.1 fixes commencement at July 15, 2002 'pending approval of permits', which both supersedes and further conditions this clause, and 4.2 measures the Contract Time from the same date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, no undefined or elastic terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the commencement date in 4.1/Addendum 4.1 but does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The number of calendar days is garbled and partially blank in the text, leaving the completion deadline unreadable on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum 4.3 substitutes a fixed date of November 30, 2003, so the two must be read together and the original day-count is displaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'Contract Sum' is defined as Cost of the Work plus Fee, but whether that sum is capped, and what 'Cost of the Work' captures given Article 7's closed list and Article 8's exclusions, is exactly the kind of payment-basis definition parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with 5.2.1, where the guaranteed maximum figure is left blank/'N/A', and with 8.1.8, 12.1.5 and 12.1.7.1, all of which compute payment by reference to a Guaranteed Maximum Price that may not exist; that is a genuine whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Fee is stated as a flat $380,000 with none of the bracketed method for adjusting the Fee for changes filled in, leaving a lump-sum fee with no stated adjustment mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 6.4 and 12.1.7.3 both contemplate either a rate or a fixed sum and supply fallback machinery, and Addendum 8.1.8 says the Fee covers listed overhead, so the clause interacts with several provisions without squarely contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative guarantee reads 'not to exceed N/A Dollars ($ N/A)', so the central number of a guaranteed-maximum-price contract is missing; whether a cap exists at all turns on that entry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1.8, 12.1.5, 12.1.6, 12.1.7.1, 13.2 and Addendum 6.5 all operate by allocating or policing a Guaranteed Maximum Price, and none of them can function if the figure is 'N/A' — a direct whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank fill-in for alternates with only boilerplate instruction text; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves blank, but the blank alternates list adds nothing of its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank heading for unit prices with no content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere depends on unit prices, and no conflicting provision appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank heading for allowances with only bracketed instructions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision allocates allowances, so the blank creates no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The assumptions underpinning the GMP are left blank, which is an absence rather than an ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 5.2.1 leaves the GMP itself blank and 5.2.6 speaks of development 'reasonably inferable', the absence of stated assumptions could matter to reconciling those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably inferable therefrom' and the exclusion of 'changes in scope, systems, kinds and quality of materials' draw a line that parties routinely dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes a priced GMP that 5.2.1 leaves blank and overlaps with Addendum 6.5's fast-track development procedure, which routes increased costs into the Cost of the Work by Change Order.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short permissive cross-reference to A201 §7.3.3 methods; nothing elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2, 6.3 and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1's change-order requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but precise definitional mapping of 'cost' and 'fee' to A201 usage, with a stated carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 6.3 and Article 7 and expressly says it shall not be modified by Articles 5, 7 and 8, which reduces rather than creates tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines the Contractor's Fee by reference to 'Subparagraph 5.1.1', but the Fee is actually stated in 5.1.2 — a cross-reference error on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mis-citation must be corrected by reading 5.1.1 and 5.1.2 together, and 13.4 makes the same mapping using 5.1.2, exposing the inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial inequity' and 'equitably adjusted' are open-textured standards with no metric supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to adjustment provisions 'in Paragraph 5.1' that were largely left blank, and it presupposes a GMP that 5.2.1 does not supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Costs necessarily incurred ... in the proper performance of the Work' and 'rates not higher than the standard paid at the place of the Project' are both judgment-laden phrases, and the closing sentence limits recovery to the enumerated Article 7 items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A and Exhibit C set contractor-owned equipment and hand-tool rates, and Addendum 8.1.8 removes several categories from reimbursement, so the boundary of the Cost of the Work is set in more than one place.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete category of wages tied to direct employment and site location.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Exhibit B's labor rate sheet and with 8.1.1's exclusion of principal-office personnel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursement turns on personnel being 'stationed at the site with the Owner's approval', a condition whose satisfaction is factual rather than textually ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1.1 excludes principal-office personnel 'except as specifically provided in 7.2.2 and 7.2.3', and Addendum 8.1.8 says the Fee covers senior management and administrative support, which narrows this item.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limited to the portion of time required for the Work; the categories are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly preserved by 8.1.1's carve-out but potentially cut back by Addendum 8.1.8's fee-covers-management list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The internal cross-reference ('Subparagraphs 7.1.1 through 7.2.j') is garbled, and 'customary benefits' is an open category illustrated by examples.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on 7.2.1-7.2.3 remaining reimbursable, which Addendum 8.1.8 partly qualifies, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain cost category with transportation and storage expressly included.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with 7.4.2, 7.5.6 and 12.1.7.2 on stored materials without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable waste and spoilage' is a soft measure but is a familiar trade standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 9.1-9.2 on credits accruing to the Owner without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Hand tools not customarily owned by construction workers' and 'fully consumed' are elastic tests, and cost for previously used items is set at 'fair market value' without a method.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C says the cost of all such hand tools shall be borne by the Contractor and substitutes a flat 5% payroll add-on, which pulls against this clause's direct-cost reimbursement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Rental charges are bounded by the Owner's prior approval of rates and quantities; the wording is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A fixes equipment rates and Exhibit C states rates for equipment not owned by Contractor are at invoiced cost, while 8.1.5 excludes rental costs except as provided here, so three documents must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, concrete cost item.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses debris removal costs differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific enumerated list closed by 'reasonable petty cash expenses of the site office'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 states the Fee covers all main-office telephone, postage, supplies, facsimiles and stationery and that none of those items are directly reimbursable under Article 7, creating a boundary dispute with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of the reasonable expenses ... incurred while travelling in discharge of duties connected with the Work' is loose but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8's list of fee-covered items and 8.1.2's exclusion of principal-office expenses both bear on which travel is reimbursable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditioned on advance Owner approval and a mutually acceptable location; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 12.1.7.2's treatment of off-site stored materials.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion ... that can be directly attributed to this Contract' requires an allocation judgment but names the test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D fixes the general liability premium at 1% of labour and subcontractor costs, a formula that may not equal the portion 'directly attributable', so the two must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sales, use or similar taxes ... related to the Work' uses a general catch-all after two specifics, though in a familiar tax formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D prescribes how Hawaii general excise tax is computed and exempts subcontract costs, which is a more detailed and potentially different rule than this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tied to permits the Contractor is required by the Contract Documents to pay for; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201's permit obligations; no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise, with two express carve-outs by cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-references to A201 13.5.3 and to 7.7.3 are consistent with those provisions as revised by the Addendum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense but specific; the sentence excluding defense costs from the Fee calculation 'or subject to the Guaranteed Maximum Price' is the only awkward passage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes an operative GMP that 5.2.1 leaves blank and cross-refers to A201 3.17.1, but nothing squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Data processing costs related to the Work' is broad and undefined, though a small-dollar category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8's list of fee-covered office and accounting expenses may swallow part of it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility', a phrase used consistently elsewhere in Article 7 and 8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels 7.7.3 and 8.1.6, which use the same formulation, so the instrument is internally consistent here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear carve-out for Owner-Contractor disputes and an express reasonableness qualifier on approval.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201's dispute provisions and with 8.1.7's residual exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Keyed to the Contractor's own 'standard personnel policy', a document not part of the Contract Documents, which leaves the measure outside the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1.1 and Addendum 8.1.8 exclude principal-office compensation and overhead, which may cut across relocation allowances for such personnel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure catch-all ('Other costs incurred in the performance of the Work') but expressly gated by advance written Owner approval.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside 8.1.7, which excludes any cost 'not specifically and expressly described in Article 7', and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1, which allows change only by Change Order, so the reach of this catch-all can be contested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete emergency category cross-referenced to A201 10.6.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum expressly revises 7.7.2 to add two limitations, so the unrevised text must be read as displaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditioned on absence of negligence and non-recoverability from insurance and others; workable though fact-intensive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum revises 7.7.3 to add an insurance-maintenance proviso, so the two versions coexist in the document and must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory line to the exclusions list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Serves as the chapeau for 8.1.1-8.1.8, which the Addendum partly rewrites, but the chapeau itself is neutral.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception 'or as may be provided in Article 14' is open-ended, and Article 14 of the Agreement contains no such provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 7.2.2 and 7.2.3, and Addendum 8.1.8 adds a further fee-covers-management rule, so the scope of excluded home-office compensation is set in three places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, categorical exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps with Addendum 8.1.8's expanded list of fee-covered office expenses but points the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Overhead and general expenses' is an accounting term of art whose boundary against Article 7's site costs is notoriously contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exception 'except as may be expressly included in Article 7' plus Addendum 8.1.8's enumeration of fee-covered overhead means two provisions define the same boundary differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow exclusion with a single express cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A's rate sheet and Exhibit C's rental provisions supply rates for Contractor-owned equipment, which must be squared with this exclusion and 7.5.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but standard fault-based exclusion with an express carve-out for 7.7.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Addendum's revision of 7.7.3 changes the carve-out's content, so the exclusion's practical reach shifts with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure expressio unius residual exclusion — 'any cost not specifically and expressly described in Article 7' — that squarely confronts Article 7's open items such as 7.7.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against 7.7.1's 'other costs approved in advance in writing' and Exhibits A-D, which add cost categories not spelled out in Article 7, the exclusion is hard to apply literally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion depends entirely on a Guaranteed Maximum Price figure, and its own wording gives no content if none exists.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2.1 leaves the GMP as 'N/A' and the First Addendum replaces 8.1.8 with an entirely different fee-covers-overhead provision, so this exclusion appears both unsupported and superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb rule for cash discounts with a clear 'otherwise' fallback, plus a specific list for trade discounts and rebates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 9.1.1 adds a seven-day notice and funding right that qualifies when the Contractor may keep discounts, so the two operate together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line accounting direction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1 and with 7.4.2's crediting mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Portions of the Work that the Contractor does not customarily perform with its own personnel' and 'reasonable objection' are both elastic tests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 6.5 sets its own bidding procedure (at least two bids, Owner-named subcontractors reasonably acceptable to Contractor), which overlaps and partly differs from this bid-delivery regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise three-condition test with a defined measure of adjustment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The remedy is an adjustment to a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves blank, and Addendum 6.5 provides a different Change Order mechanism keyed to the Contract Sum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple period definition with an unfilled 'or as follows' alternative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 12.1.3's application deadlines and Addendum 12.1.4's added submittals without conflict.
